execution_model.description: v0.19 organizes the entire HyperQL API around four foundational concepts [Decision 14].

the_four_concept_model.description: Declare fields, node types, edge types, traits, views, unions, and other schema constructs. Immediate and synchronous.
Describe a query via QueryBuilder. Returns a QueryPlan value. No I/O.
Execute a QueryPlan. Returns typed result rows. Consumes I/O.
Scope mutation operations atomically within a transaction boundary.

query_plan.description: A first-class, storable, and immutable value type containing a validated QueryNode tree, its parameter bindings, and its dependency set of SchemaIds.
query_plan.lifecyle: Produced by .plan(). Fully validated at plan time. Storable and reusable. Valid subject for explain() and analyze().
fields: dependency_set: []SchemaId /* the complete set of all schema constructs (types, fields, roles, etc.) referenced by this plan. Includes Node<T> type references. Used for revalidation on schema ALTER.
query_plan.revalidation_on_alter: Schema ALTER triggers synchronous plan revalidation [Decision 10]. Plans are moved to 'invalid' if revalidation fails (e.g., a dependency SchemaId is retired via DROP).

plan_and_run_api.run_method: db.run(QueryPlan) or db.match(...).run() -> returns typed result rows.
plan_and_run_api.semantics: .run() is sugar over .plan().run(). Both paths execute identically.

abstract_rules: Caller is responsible for the lifetime of result data.
Result data is valid until caller explicitly releases it.
Results from one .run() do not share storage with results from another.
A QueryPlan does not hold or extend the lifetime of any result data.
result_ownership.concrete_mechanisms: Deferred to per-language binding guides (RAII, GC, ARC, etc.) [Decision 2].

transaction_management.description: HyperQL supports ACID transactions with configurable isolation levels. Single statements and batch forms are automatically wrapped in transactions.

error_model.philosophy: Strict/Abort. Any error aborts the entire transaction immediately.
error_model.behavior: No partial commits. If any statement in a transaction fails, all previous operations in that transaction are rolled back.
error_model.batch_atomicity: v0.19 batch forms ([...]) are implicitly atomic. An error in any entry (e.g., one node in CREATE NODE [...]) rolls back the entire statement.
error_model.rationale: Ensures data consistency and predictable application state.

constraint_violations.timing: Constraints are validated in order: Node -> Referential Integrity (Node<T>) -> Cardinality -> Role -> Edge
constraint_violations.atomicity: All constraints for a level must pass before proceeding to next level
constraint_violations.error_codes: [3011] Node, [4001] Referential Integrity (deletion blocked), [3014] Cardinality, [3012] Role, [3013] Edge
constraint_violations.rollback: Any violation triggers full transaction rollback unless ON ERROR CONTINUE is set.

isolation_levels.minimum_floor: Implementations MUST provide at minimum READ_COMMITTED semantics at the session level. Weaker session-level isolation is not permitted.
isolation_levels.pluggable_model: Spec defines isolation semantics; implementations choose synchronization models (locking, MVCC, OCC) [Decision 3].

levels.description: Default. Reads observe only committed data. Snapshot taken at statement start.
All reads within a transaction observe the same snapshot. Phantom reads possible.
Full isolation. Transactions execute as if serialized.

write_conflicts.error: Transaction rolled back due to concurrent modification conflict [5002]

deadlock_detection.resolution: One transaction is chosen as victim and rolled back [5001]

batch_syntax_hierarchy.level_2: Batch of same type using [ ] (e.g., DEFINE NODE [ Person { ... }, Dog { ... } ];)
batch_syntax_hierarchy.level_3: Batch of mixed types using nested [ ] (e.g., DEFINE [ FIELD [ ... ], NODE [ ... ] ];)

batch_processing.atomicity: Implicitly atomic. Error in any entry rolls back the entire batch statement.
batch_processing.shared_scope: Batch CREATE [NODE [...], EDGE [...]] shares variable scope between sub-blocks for atomic cross-type creation.

error_mode.description: Transaction mode that allows execution to continue after statement failures. Must be set at BEGIN. Enables partial success in bulk loads.
formal_semantics: Individual statement failures do not abort the transaction.
Failed statements are skipped; execution continues with the next statement.
Each failure is appended to the transaction error log.
At COMMIT, a TransactionResult is returned containing counts and error detail.
Only successful statements are committed. Failed statements produce no mutations.
ROLLBACK discards all work including successful statements.

TransactionResult.skipped: Int /* statements skipped due to errors

StatementError.statement_index: u64 /* 0-based position within the transaction (or block)

constraint_performance.description: Performance characteristics of the three-level constraint system.

write_operations.overhead: Microseconds per constraint for simple expressions
write_operations.bulk_operations: Constraint checking amortized across transaction - use BEGIN/COMMIT for batching
write_operations.evaluation_order: Node -> Role -> Edge constraints evaluated in sequence

read_operations.validation_timing: Zero - constraints are never re-evaluated during reads
read_operations.guarantee: Data integrity ensured by write-time validation
read_operations.performance_impact: None - reads operate on pre-validated data
read_operations.benefit: Eliminates need for application-level validation on reads. Node<T> field constraints allow direct child field validation without needing @computed(TRAVERSE) or @materialized.

computed_properties.policy: Constraints on @computed fields are not supported in v0.20
computed_properties.rationale: Computed properties are calculated at read-time; enforcing constraints would add read overhead
computed_properties.workaround: Use node/edge constraints to validate relationships that determine computed values

indirect_benefits.indexes: @unique decorator creates indexes that improve read performance
indirect_benefits.data_quality: Guaranteed valid data reduces defensive programming overhead
indirect_benefits.query_optimization: Constraint guarantees enable query planner optimizations

performance_warnings.description: Static analysis warnings emitted by the query planner to signal inefficient patterns.

WARN-PERF-001.trigger: @computed(TRAVERSE) in WHERE clause without selective predicates.
WARN-PERF-001.message: Computed property in WHERE clause will execute subquery for each scanned row. Materialize for production.

WARN-PERF-002.trigger: UDF in WHERE clause without selective index-backed predicates.

WARN-PERF-004.message: Emitted when a CROSS_TYPE query falls back to a scan because of stale/missing views, or when a @computed(TRAVERSE) @materialized field has incomplete write-trigger derivation.

performance_model.description: Detailed performance characteristics of HyperQL operations

index_usage.automatic_selection: Query planner automatically uses indexes when available and beneficial
conditions_for_use: Equality predicates (WHERE field = value) - Uses index if available
Range predicates (WHERE field > value) - B-tree indexes only
IN clauses (WHERE field IN [values]) - Index lookup per value
Composite index prefix (WHERE LastName = 'X' AND FirstName = 'Y') - Uses composite index on (LastName, FirstName)
not_used_when: No index exists on filtered field
Predicate uses function (WHERE UPPER(name) = 'X') - Bypasses index
Low selectivity (WHERE gender = 'M' on 50/50 split) - Full scan may be faster
OR predicates across different fields (WHERE age > 30 OR name = 'X')
index_usage.verification: Use EXPLAIN to confirm index usage

traverse_default.read_cost: Subquery execution per row (first access), cached thereafter within a single query execution

traverse_materialized.write_cost: Recomputation on write triggers derived from QueryPlan
traverse_materialized.update_triggers: CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE of edges in traversal pattern

udf_performance.execution_model: UDFs are interpreted at runtime, not compiled.

scalar_pure.use_case: Result formatting, data validation in constraints.

readonly_traversal.cost: Interpreter overhead PLUS the cost of the underlying MATCH traversal.
readonly_traversal.warning: Always emits [WARN-PERF-002] when used in a WHERE clause regardless of selectivity, as interpreter overhead compounds traversal cost.

high_volume_scans.behavior: Any UDF in a WHERE clause without selective index-backed predicates will emit [WARN-PERF-002].
high_volume_scans.recommendation: Prefer built-in operators for filtering large result sets.

transaction_log_growth.description: Transaction log size grows with operation count and data volume
factors: Size of modified data (large strings, lists)
mitigation: Avoid updating large text fields in loops
Use BATCH with ON ERROR CONTINUE for bulk loads

medium_batch.example: FOR each 1000 records: BEGIN; CREATE...; COMMIT;

large_batch.example: -- Split data into partitions, run concurrent transactions

recommendations: Disable indexes during bulk load, rebuild after (future feature)
Use ON ERROR CONTINUE to skip failures without rollback
Sort data by indexed fields before insert for better locality
Monitor transaction log size and memory usage

query_planning.description: HyperQL uses a cost-based optimizer with storage-aware planning.

rules: WITH is a hard barrier: variables not explicitly listed are dropped from scope.
Shadowing is FORBIDDEN: Cannot redefine a variable already in scope.
Batch Scope: Variables bound in a NODE sub-block are in scope for the EDGE sub-block within the same statement.

storage_aware_planning.late_materialization: The optimizer delays loading variable-width heap data until after all filter predicates have been applied.
storage_aware_planning.materialized_view_usage: Queries whose predicates match a Materialized View's index fields automatically use the view instead of cross-partition scans.

selection_criteria.description: Index must match WHERE clause types.
@index(vector) uses SoA layout for SIMD-accelerated similarity.

strategies.name: Index Nested Loop
strategies.preferred: Default for role-based edge traversal using Role Index Tables

path_query_optimization.description: Special optimizations for MATCH PATH queries

techniques.name: Cost-based path selection
techniques.description: Algorithm selected based on WEIGHT BY aggregation (Sum=A*, Max=Bottleneck, Min=Widest).

statistics_and_maintenance.automatic: Statistics auto-updated on significant data changes.

bulk_operations.description: For inserting or updating large datasets efficiently

transaction_batching.description: Group multiple operations into single transaction for better performance
benefits: Reduced transaction overhead (single commit vs thousands)
transaction_batching.example: BEGIN; CREATE NODE [ p1:Person {...}, p2:Person {...} ]; COMMIT;

parameterized_batching.description: Use query parameters for repeated operations
parameterized_batching.notes: Parameterized queries allow query plan caching and better performance

csv_json_extensions.rationale: CSV/JSON import could be built-in functions or extensions. Currently evaluating whether these should be core features or plugins.
csv_json_extensions.workaround: Use application-level batch processing with BEGIN/COMMIT transactions
csv_json_extensions.potential_syntax:
LOAD CSV FROM 'file.csv' AS row
CREATE NODE p:Person { Name: row.name, Age: TO_INT(row.age) };
